messages.subject: Re: Categorical variable with no threshold
parts:
Hm, difficult to say without seeing the data.

My first guess was that you have missing data, and after listwise
deletion, ipmodst only has one category left. But then you would get the
error message:

lavaan ERROR: ordered variable(s) has/have only 1 level

together with a varTable showing you the problematic variable. So it
must be something else. Do you get any other warnings?

The best way for us to diagnose the problem is to get the data (or a
snippet of the data, just large enough to reproduce the problem), and
the full R script).

Yves.

On 06/11/2016 09:06 PM, Ugo Leonard wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I am doing this work on a dataset containing solely categorical
> variables. The model (called model4) specified is the following:
>
> SD =~ ipcrtiv + impfree
> UNBE =~ ipeqopt + ipudrst + impenv + iphlppl + iplylfr +imprich +impdiff
> COTR =~ ipfrule + ipbhprp + ipmodst + imptrad
> SEC =~ impsafe + ipstrgv
> POAC =~ imprich + iprspot + ipshabt + ipsuces
> HE =~ ipgdtim + impfun
> ST =~ impdiff + ipadvnt + iprspot
>
>
> When looking at the output of
>
> cfa_be <- cfa(model=model4, data=be, ordered=vars)
>
> where "vars" is
>
> vars <- c("ipcrtiv", "impfree", "ipeqopt", "ipudrst", "impenv",
> "iphlppl", "iplylfr", "ipfrule","ipbhprp", "ipmodst", "imptrad",
> "impsafe", "ipstrgv", "imprich", "iprspot", "ipshabt","ipsuces",
> "ipgdtim", "impfun", "impdiff", "ipadvnt")
>
> a vector specifying that all variables are categorical, it appears that
> the variable /ipmodst/ for /COTR/ is an intercept and does not have any
> thresholds. Would anybody happen to have an idea why this occured?
>
> This variable is not constant in my dataset so it should have thresholds
> like the other variables, I think.
>
> Thank you for your help !
>
> Ugo
